newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest has slow day for currency futures.
newsitem.headline: Budapest has slow day for currency futures.

text.p: Currency futures on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) had a relatively slow day on Wednesday with interest centring around the yen, although trading revived on the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE).
The BCE saw 3.19 billion forints turnover, with one third made up by yen, while the BSE saw a substantial 2.08 billion forints, consisting mainly of agency crosses in marks and dollars, dealers said.
"There's a lot of position covering as the forint/yen spot rate has gone up five forints in the last 10 days," said Gabor Herczeg of LaSalle. @
"On the one hand people are betting against yen interest rates as they calculate the differential between them and the forint's devaluation," he said.
"And on the other hand there are people who didn't believe 122 yen to the dollar was a barrier, bet against it coming down as it has done and are now covering their short postions."
On the BCE, the Decmeber yen rose 85 fillers to 166.60 forints per 100 yen while the December mark fell 25 fillers to 112.50 fpritns. @
The BSE saw three contracts for the March 1997 mark worth a total 1.33 forints and three for March dollars at 574 million forints.
"It was probably an agency cross," said Gyula Fulop of Mezobank Broker. "The BSE is not at all liquid at the moment as people are still nervous about the strong dollar."

Herczeg said there was increasing evidence on both markets of basket-structured forint transactions whereby marks and dollars are bought or sold in quantities proportionate to the currency basket against which the forint floats on the spot market. @
The basket is made up 70 percent of the mark and 30 percent of the dollar.
"This (structure) was quite a feature of last year's markets but had disappeared until recently," Herczeg said.
On the BSE the mark fell 59 fillers to 104.16 forints for March and by five fillers to 116.1 forints for December.
The dollar rose 38 fillers forints to 176.22 forints for March and by 65 fillers to 184.5 forints for September.
